source_candidate.candidate: OpenDHT raw 20-byte InfoHash lookup keyed by exact Git SHA-1 plus local Git canonical-object verification

verified_points: HASH_LEN is 20 and InfoHash is Hash<HASH_LEN>.
Hash(const uint8_t*, size_t) calls fromBytes, and fromBytes copies the first N bytes directly when at least N bytes are supplied.
Hash::get(const uint8_t*, size_t) is a separate operation that invokes crypto::hash, so hashing is not mandatory when the raw-byte constructor is used.
DhtRunner exposes get overloads taking InfoHash directly.
DhtRunner also exposes put overloads taking InfoHash, so retrieval and publication are separate API operations.
DhtRunner::run binds a local DHT node/network execution context; passive retrieval therefore still requires an actual OpenDHT network client execution surface.
The low-level search API accepts const InfoHash& id.
Search/get and announce/publication are distinct operations.
For non-delta objects Git formats the object header, initializes the repository hash, hashes the header, then hashes the inflated object bytes before finalizing the object id.
Loose-object validation recomputes the object hash from the decoded header/content stream and rejects when the recomputed oid differs from the expected oid.

verified_claims.claim: An exact 20-byte Git SHA-1 can be represented as an OpenDHT InfoHash without mandatory rehashing.
verified_claims.reason: InfoHash is exactly 20 bytes, the raw-byte Hash constructor copies those bytes directly, and hashing occurs only through the separate Hash::get API.

verified_claims.claim: OpenDHT retrieval APIs can receive that raw InfoHash directly as the lookup key.
verified_claims.reason: DhtRunner and lower-level DHT search/get APIs accept InfoHash values directly.

verified_claims.claim: Returned candidate Git object bytes can be locally rejected if they do not match the expected Git object id.
verified_claims.reason: Git hashes the canonical object header plus object data and its loose-object validation rejects an expected/recomputed oid mismatch.

verified_claims.claim: The source-level exact-key bridge by itself proves a passive scheduled-Chat route to the target Git object.
verified_claims.reason: No independent evidence establishes that the target payload already exists under that OpenDHT key, and this run has no exposed OpenDHT/UDP/DhtRunner execution surface with which to perform the network lookup.
